title: Sulking
note: With neither heart hurrying to union and both meaning to sulk, the two sulk with each other. That also explains the chapter’s place here.

couplets.plain: Don’t embrace him. Sulk, and let us see a little of the pain and sickness he goes through.
couplets.pm: If you sulk, we can see a little of the painful sickness of desire he will suffer. Don’t hurry to embrace him. Keep this up. She says “a little” because a sulk mustn’t be drawn out. Seeing the sulk, she takes her side and teases: he should feel a little of what we felt. In this way she brings her round.
couplets.context: Her friend has come as his go-between. She teases her, to win her over to accepting him.
couplets.speaker: maid

links.reason: The maid urges a sulk for the sport of seeing him suffer a little.

couplets.plain: A sulk is like the right amount of salt. Drawing it out is like a little too much.
couplets.pm: A sulk should be just enough to make union sweet, as salt is just enough to make food taste good. Stretching it even slightly past that is like too much salt. Stretching it means not knowing the measure, and going on until the impulse towards union fades. Too much salt spoils the taste, and too much sulking spoils the joy of union.
couplets.context: Her friend says this so that she will give up sulking and accept him.
couplets.speaker: maid

links.quote: A sulk is like the right amount of salt.
links.reason: Says what the sulk is: the seasoning of union, good only in small measure.

links.quote: Drawing it out is like a little too much.

couplets.plain: Not to embrace those who sulk with you is like bringing fresh pain to people already in distress.
couplets.pm: For a man to walk away without ending the sulk of women who sulk at not having him is like bringing worse pain on those already ruined by it. She means: you go to others, so the courtesans sulk at not having you. If you don’t go and end their sulk and embrace them, they won’t be able to bear it.
couplets.note: He hears this as bitter irony. The women she means are the courtesans, and she is sending him back to them.
couplets.context: He has come back from the courtesans, and she sulks with him and says this.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Not to embrace those who sulk with you
links.reason: Said to the man’s face: leaving a sulking woman unembraced adds to her pain.

links.quote: like bringing fresh pain to people already in distress

couplets.plain: Not to soothe those who sulk is like cutting a withered creeper at the root.
couplets.pm: Not soothing and joining the courtesans who sulk with you is like cutting at the root a creeper already withered for want of water. When you are with them, we should comfort ourselves with our son. We have no right to sulk with you, so you needn’t soothe us. Soothe the courtesans, who have that right. So go there.
couplets.note: He hears irony again. She says she has no right to sulk, and sends him to the courtesans, who have.
couplets.context: She goes on, sulking with him.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: cutting a withered creeper at the root
links.reason: Shows what refusing to make up does: it cuts at the root of something already withering.

links.quote: cutting a withered creeper at the root
links.reason: Leaving someone’s sulk unsoothed cuts at the root a creeper already withered.

couplets.plain: What graces those of fine character is the sulking in the hearts of women with eyes like flowers.
couplets.pm: What graces even leaders of fine character is the great sulking in the hearts of women with eyes like flowers. “Even” shows that a sulk is sweet to those with no fault. The grace lies in reaching its reward of joy. He is marvelling at the sulk that brought him the joy he has just had.
couplets.context: He has ended her sulk and been with her, and he says this to himself.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: What graces those of fine character
links.reason: Grants the sulk a grace that adorns even those of fine character.

couplets.plain: Without the deep sulk and the light one, desire is like a fruit too ripe and a fruit too green.
couplets.pm: If there is no deep quarrel and no light quarrel, desire is like a fruit past its best and a young green fruit. Fruit so ripe it is about to fall gives little pleasure, so without the deep one desire is that. Hard green fruit isn’t ready to enjoy, so without the light one desire is that. He is praising the need for both.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: Without the deep sulk and the light one
links.reason: Treats deep and light sulks as what desire can’t do without.

links.quote: a fruit too ripe and a fruit too green
links.reason: Desire without sulking is fruit gone past its best, or fruit too green to eat.

couplets.plain: There is a pain even in sulking: the worry over whether union will be delayed.
couplets.pm: Even in a sulk, which joy can’t do without, there is a pain, from wondering whether union will be delayed or not. So a sulk makes you hurry towards union.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: There is a pain even in sulking

couplets.plain: What is the use of suffering, when there is no lover to know you are suffering?
couplets.pm: If you don’t have someone with loving-kindness who knows you are suffering for their sake, what use is suffering? To know here is to understand a sulk well. She isn’t my beloved, so she doesn’t know this pain, and so my sulking is useless. In this way he shows that he can’t bear it.
couplets.context: She won’t give up her sulk, so he sulks back at her and says this.
couplets.speaker: he

couplets.plain: Water is sweet in the shade, and sulking is sweet with those who love you.
couplets.pm: Water, vital to life, is sweet in the shade and not in the sun. So too sulking, vital to union, is sweet with those who have loving-kindness and not with those who don’t. Those who love you are pained by your suffering and long to join you. She has neither of these for me, so even this sulk turns bitter.
couplets.context: He goes on, sulking with her.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: sulking is sweet with those who love you
links.reason: Sets its test: a sulk is sweet only with those who love you.

couplets.plain: My heart says we will join with the one who leaves a sulk to wither. That is only craving.
couplets.pm: She can leave things so, even as she withers in her sulk. My heart tries to join such a woman only out of its own craving, and nothing else. To think someone has loving-kindness and compassion when she has neither, and to try to join her, is what craving does. This union won’t happen.
couplets.context: He goes on, sulking with her.
couplets.speaker: he

links.reason: Brands his own yearning for a woman who leaves a sulk to wither as mere craving.

ideaLinks.quote: sulking is sweet with those who love you
ideaLinks.reason: A sulk has its sweetness only with those who love you, as water has its sweetness in the shade.

ideaLinks.quote: Without the deep sulk and the light one, desire is like a fruit too ripe and a fruit too green.
ideaLinks.reason: Without sulks deep and light, desire is fruit too ripe or too green.
